editorial:
Imagine moving your whole life to a city where nobody wants you, all because you believe in a dream that is already dead. You follow an army officer who stays loyal to Yugoslavia even as the country splits apart. He moves his family to Belgrade, thinking it is the right thing to do, but he quickly finds out that being an outsider in a war-torn place is a nightmare. The vibe is heavy and sad, showing you how a man's pride and loyalty can actually destroy the people he loves the most. It feels like watching a slow train wreck where you want to scream at the screen for him to just give up and leave.

The acting is the best part here because you can really feel the stress and anger in every scene. While the pacing is a bit slow at times, the emotional payoff is worth it. If you like stories about family drama mixed with real-life history, you will love this.
endingExplained: Everything falls apart when the officer realizes his loyalty was for nothing. His family reaches a breaking point and they cannot fix the damage done by the war and his stubbornness. The movie ends with a feeling of total loss. He is left alone in a city that never accepted him, showing that sticking to an old idea can leave you with nothing but regrets and an empty home.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves historical dramas and family stories.
